column1: # pulse-infra dependency registry
# THE DIRECTION OF THIS FILE IS THE POINT. pulse-infra provides backing services
# and nothing else: it does not build, start, configure or test another repo's
# code. Projects that need infrastructure REGISTER it here, and this stack
# provisions it. Nothing in this repo reaches back into a consumer.
# To register a dependency: add a row, open a PR against pulse-infra. Adding a
# row is a stack-contract change — see "Changing this contract" in
# docs/stack-contract.md. The row and the code that uses it land together.
# Columns are whitespace-separated. Four fields, all required, no free text:
#   kind       what is being registered (see below)
#   name       the topic / bucket / key / port number
#   owner      project(s) that break if it is missing; comma-separated, no spaces
#   spec       kind-specific; "-" means "stack defaults"
# Kinds, and what this stack does with each:
#   topic      PROVISIONED by bootstrap/bootstrap.sh at `make up`.
#              spec: partitions=N to override, or "-" for TOPIC_PARTITIONS.
#              Replication factor and min ISR always come from the profile, so
#              the same row works on core/full (RF=3) and lite (RF=1).
#   bucket     PROVISIONED by bootstrap. spec is always "-".
#   redis-key  DECLARED only. Redis keys spring into being on first write, so
#              there is nothing to create; the row records who writes it and
#              stops two projects colliding on a name. spec: stream | list.
#   port       RESERVED only. This stack does not run the listener — the owner
#              does. The row exists so port numbers cannot be handed out twice,
#              which is how 9090 was known to be free. spec: the protocol.
# Provisioning is idempotent: a topic or bucket that already exists is left
# exactly as it is, never recreated or reconfigured.
# kind       name                  owner                          spec
# Names deliberately mirror the Redis key names below, so one vocabulary covers
# both transports. 6 partitions divides evenly by 1, 2, 3 and 6 consumers, so
# consumer-group rebalancing is observable at every group size worth trying.
topic        ingestion-events      pulse-ingestor,pulse-gateway   partitions=6
topic        ingestion-signals     pulse-ingestor,pulse-gateway   partitions=6
topic        ingestion-logs        pulse-ingestor,pulse-gateway   partitions=6
# "staging", not "bronze": a transient landing pad with no retention promise.
# Object paths are a convention, not pre-created directories — GCS has none.
bucket       pulse-staging-local   pulse-ingestor                 -
# Declared, not created. Structure is the owner's contract with its consumers;
# this stack only guarantees a Redis that honours it.
redis-key    ingestion-events      pulse-gateway,pulse-conflux    stream
redis-key    ingestion-signals     pulse-gateway,pulse-conflux    stream
redis-key    ingestion-logs        pulse-gateway,pulse-conflux    list
redis-key    ingestion-dlq         pulse-gateway                  list
# Reserved, not served. The owner runs the listener in its own compose file.
port         8080                  pulse-gateway                  http
port         9090                  pulse-gateway                  grpc
port         8090                  pulse-conflux                  http
